//: THE SECTION-TO-PART CONTRACT. Hand-written, and NOTHING regenerates it — that is the entire
point of the file. assets/whitepaper.parts.json records the same mapping but is rewritten by the
same run of tools/paper-to-text.mjs that moves a boundary, so it agrees with every move and can
never witness its own drift. This file can, because changing it is a separate human act.
WHY A MAPPING AND NOT A COUNT. tools/paper-to-text.mjs packs sections greedily against a 55,000
byte budget at section boundaries. Measured 29 July 2026: part 4 sat 173 bytes under budget, and
adding 465 bytes to section 6 moved section 8 (Limitations and Honest Disclosures) out of part 4
and into part 5 while the count stayed at seven. Every check in this repository watched the
count, so all of them stayed green through that move, while every citation telling a reader that
part 4 carries the limitations silently became wrong. The count is not the contract; this is.
'sections' is what the splitter must produce, joined with two spaces, a pipe and two spaces.
'publications' is every place the mapping is stated in prose. Each 'mustContain' string is
matched BYTE FOR BYTE, deliberately: keyword-matching prose against generated headings was tried
on paper and rejected, because part 2 is published as 'the twenty-two services' and generated as
'4. Service Catalogue', and no keyword rule relates those without either false-positiving or
being loosened until it matches anything. Storing both sides verbatim asserts the weaker but
checkable property: the pairing a human approved is still the pairing being served AND the
pairing being published, and neither side may move without the other.
TO CHANGE THE PAPER'S SHAPE ON PURPOSE: regenerate, run `npm run gate:y`, read what it says
moved, decide whether the published descriptions are still true of the new mapping, then update
BOTH this file and every publication it names. If that feels like friction, it is the friction
that was missing when assets/landing.html went on telling readers the paper had six parts.

sections: 10. The Build: Story, Process, and a User Scenario
11. Roadmap: Operating Quiver After the Hackathon
